id_and_class.theory_title: Hurley’s Sensorimotor Loops and Embodied Interaction
id_and_class.summary: Susan Hurley rejects the ‘sandwich model’ that puts cognition between perceptual input and behavioral output, arguing that perception and action are deeply interdependent. Consciousness emerges from dynamic sensorimotor feedback loops between an embodied agent and its world, and its vehicles may extend beyond the brain into body and environment.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a dynamic process of perception and action that co-constitute each other through embodied interaction, not an inner theater of representations processed in isolation.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Personal-level interdependence of experience and agency emerges from subpersonal causal processes and complex dynamic feedback systems that span brain, body and environment.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence (personal-level experience from subpersonal dynamic feedback systems)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Hurley ties the unity of a conscious perspective to agency. In her words, the self ‘no longer lurks hidden somewhere between perceptual input and behavioral output, but reappears out in the open, embodied and embedded in its environment.’
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Embodied agents, sensorimotor feedback loops, subpersonal causal and dynamic systems, and an environment that can host vehicles of mental content.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through philosophical analysis informed by neuroscience and the social sciences, using control systems theory and dynamical systems as models.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A two-level structure: a personal level of mental contents and norms, and a subpersonal level of causal processes and feedback systems linking perception and action.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Unity of perspective, Self-consciousness, Agency, Perception
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Two-way sensorimotor feedback: action shapes perception as much as perception guides action, in continuous real-time loops with the environment.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness is a continuous dynamic process sustained by ongoing interaction, not a static product of central processing.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Possibly distributed across brain, body and environment; Hurley’s vehicle externalism allows the vehicles of mental content to extend beyond the brain.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness is embedded in action and context; agency helps constitute the unity of the conscious perspective.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: The unity of a conscious perspective depends on agency and the interdependence of perception and action.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Information flows in both directions between perception and action, which challenges linear, input-output models of conscious processing.
core_claims_and_evidence: The sandwich model artificially separates perception, cognition and action, which are deeply interdependent.
Control systems theory and dynamical systems model consciousness better than static computational models.
The vehicles of mental content, not only the content, can extend into body and environment.
Agency plays a role in the unity of a conscious perspective.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical, informed by neuroscience, control theory and dynamical systems

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Hurley’s view is less a classical theory than a reconception of how consciousness arises, so it gives no specific mechanism for phenomenal experience.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: If perception and action co-constitute consciousness, it is unclear where exactly the mind stops.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent with naturalism and dynamical systems science; vehicle externalism departs from brain-bound physicalism without leaving physicalism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since consciousness depends on sensorimotor loops rather than a particular substrate, an artificial agent might qualify if it is embodied and acts in real-time interaction with an environment.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Consciousness here is a process of an embodied, acting agent, so it ends when the body can no longer perceive and act.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A static copy of brain states would leave out the body–world loops that, on this view, constitute consciousness.
